title: CDC Proofs for Masking with Shuffling
summary: CDC-based proofs cover masking alone; proving security for masking combined with shuffling and whether it lowers the required physical-noise level remain open.

formal_statement.body: Develop a formal security proof using the CDC/Doeblin-coefficient framework for implementations that combine masking with shuffling, and determine whether this combination can lower the physical-noise level required to obtain relevant security parameters.

scope.domain: Side-channel security of masked-and-shuffled implementations in the noisy leakage model using CDC/Doeblin coefficients.
parameters: physical-noise level — requirement whose possible reduction is being assessed
security parameters — target values for which the physical-noise requirement is evaluated
scope.unresolved_remainder: Develop a CDC-based formal proof for masking combined with shuffling and determine whether the combination lowers the physical-noise level needed for relevant security parameters.

citations.label: Formal Security Proofs via Doeblin Coefficients: Optimal Side-channel Factorization from Noisy Leakage to Random Probing

progress.summary: The paper presents this as a perspective extending CDC-based proofs for masking alone, leaving the combined proof and possible noise reduction for future investigation.
citation_labels: Julien Béguinot et al., Formal Security Proofs via Doeblin Coefficients: Optimal Side-channel Factorization from Noisy Leakage to Random Probing
